slides.texte_overlay:
7 ways to rescue an
awkward moment that
feel like a cheat code
Forgot someone's name right after hearing it? Introduce them to a friend. "Have you met Tom?" They'll usually say their own name back while shaking hands, problem solved.
Said something that landed wrong? Name it straight away. "That came out weird, what I meant was..." Owning it in the moment makes it disappear almost instantly.
Went in for a handshake and they went for a hug? Just laugh and say "Let's do both." Turning the mix-up into a joke makes it a funny moment, not an awkward one.
Called someone by the wrong name? Apologise once, use the right name twice in the next minute, and move on. Repeating it shows you care without making a scene.
When the conversation dies, bring a story. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and I've always got something fun ready to restart the chat.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. When a conversation dies, I've always got a fun story to restart it.

slides.texte_overlay: Spilled your drink on the table? Say "Well, that's my party trick" and help clean up. Calm and funny in a small disaster makes people like you even more than before.
Nobody laughed at your joke? Smile and say "That was funnier in my head." Self-awareness is funnier than the joke would have been, and the moment passes easily.
